title: At the clinic
setting: You've had a fever and a cough for a few days, so you've gone to a clinic (klinik) near where you're staying. The doctor calls you in.

n1.speaker: doctor
n1.english: Have a seat. What seems to be the problem?

options.english: I've got a fever and a cough, doctor.
options.feedback: Clear: the symptoms straight after saya, and Dok to address the doctor.
Everyone knows masuk angin, but it's a folk name for feeling off. Give the doctor the symptoms: Saya demam dan batuk.

options.english: I have a fever and a cough.
options.feedback: Word for word from English. Symptoms don't take punya: Saya demam dan batuk.

n2.speaker: doctor
n2.english: How long have you had it?

options.feedback: Sudah plus the time says it's been going on that long, and still is.

options.indonesian: Demamnya sejak Senin, Dok. Batuknya baru kemarin.
options.english: The fever since Monday. The cough only since yesterday.
options.feedback: Sejak (since) before the day, and baru for 'only just': precise and useful.

options.indonesian: Saya demam tiga hari yang lalu.
options.english: I had a fever three days ago.
options.feedback: This sounds as if the fever was three days ago and is over. Sudah tiga hari (it's been three days) says it's still going.

n3.speaker: doctor
n3.english: Are you allergic to any medicines?

options.feedback: The medicine goes straight after alergi, with no word for 'to'. Always say it before anything is prescribed.
An ada question is answered ada or tidak ada: a clear no.
Ke is 'to' for places you go. Alergi goes straight before the thing: alergi penisilin.

n4.speaker: doctor
n4.english: Your throat's inflamed. It looks like a viral infection.

options.feedback: A fair question, and Dok keeps it polite.
Perlu …? asks whether something is needed: a good question before you're handed a bag of pills.
Too blunt with a doctor, and antibiotics don't touch a virus. Ask instead: Perlu antibiotik, Dok?

n5.speaker: doctor
n5.indonesian: Tidak serius, dan tidak perlu antibiotik. Ini obat penurun panas dan obat batuk. Diminum tiga kali sehari, sesudah makan.
n5.english: It's not serious, and you don't need antibiotics. This is for the fever, and this is a cough medicine. Take them three times a day, after meals.

options.indonesian: Tiga kali sehari, sesudah makan, ya, Dok?
options.english: Three times a day after meals, right?
options.feedback: Repeating the dose back is the best way to check you heard it right.
The doctor has just said it: sesudah makan, after meals. Listen for sebelum (before) and sesudah (after), then repeat it back.

options.indonesian: Kalau demamnya tidak turun, bagaimana, Dok?
options.english: What if the fever doesn't come down?
options.feedback: Kalau … bagaimana? asks what to do if something happens: sensible to ask before you leave.

n6.speaker: doctor
n6.indonesian: Banyak istirahat dan minum air putih, ya. Kalau tiga hari lagi belum sembuh, kontrol lagi.
n6.english: Get plenty of rest and drink lots of water. If you're not better in three days, come back and see me.

options.feedback: Baik (all right) is the polite way to show you've taken instructions in.
If work needs one, ask now, before you pay: clinics are used to it.
Said quickly, iya, iya sounds like 'yeah, yeah, I know'. Baik, Dok and a thank you shows you've listened.

end.speaker: narration
end.english: Done. Symptoms go straight after saya (Saya demam, with no punya), sudah or sejak says how long, alergi takes the thing straight after it, and the dose comes as diminum … kali sehari. Call the doctor Dok, and repeat the instructions back.
